question.text: As per SEBI's 2020 circular, mutual fund schemes that are being wound up must be:

answer.text: Listed on stock exchanges to provide exit route to investors during the interim period
Merged with another scheme of the same AMC
Kept in suspended mode until market conditions improve

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's May 2020 circular requires schemes that are being wound up to be listed on stock exchanges so that investors have an interim exit route and access to liquidity during the wind-up period. The Trap: Winding up is not the same as instant liquidation; the disposal of assets can take time, and listing is the mechanism that provides interim liquidity. Note: The interim listing requirement is an investor-protection measure to ensure exit availability during the wind-up process.
